comment: The cases ziptz_test.go and test_ziptz.py both run, so the two libraries
are held to one list rather than to two that can drift. Each case has a
token and exactly one expectation: "zone", the IANA name it resolves to,
or "error", the kind of failure it must produce -- "malformed" for a
token that is not three or five ASCII digits, "unassigned" for a real
looking prefix the Postal Service has never assigned.
"why" is documentation, not an assertion. A why beginning "known gap"
marks an answer that is wrong or missing and understood to be so; those
are pinned here deliberately, so that fixing one fails this file and
makes someone update it.
"zones" is the same idea for the other three answers: one representative
ZIP per zone, the generic name it must give, and the abbreviation it must
give at each instant in "instants" -- one in January, one in July, so a
zone that observes daylight saving is caught doing it. Every zone the
tables can return must appear, and the suites fail if one is missing.
Add a case here and both suites pick it up with no other edit.
"tables" is what the generated tables should contain, and "checks" names
every property both suites have to test. Cases alone were not enough: the
structural checks around them were written twice, once per language, and
two hand-written lists drift -- one suite had a check on the exception
suffixes being in order for a while before the other did. Now the list
lives here, each suite maps every name to a test, and a suite missing a
name fails rather than quietly testing less than the other.
"language_only" is for what genuinely cannot be shared: Go has no default
arguments, and only Python can be imported two ways.
